You found a second, different bug - and card 10 would not have fixed it.

Card 4 made the row draggable by its name, and that part works. You do not grab rows by the name. You grab them at the edges, and those still did nothing.

MEASURED on the build you are running (2026-11-03 16:23), dragging Craig payment? from the bottom of four rows to the top, logging every event:

where you grab itdrag starts?drop accepted?result
the square (checkbox)yesnonothing moves
the far left edgeyesnonothing moves

the nameyesyesmoves
Notice the middle column: the drag started every single time. That is what makes this a different bug from card 4, where the drag never started at all. Here the row lifts, you move it, you let go — and the row you are aiming at refuses the drop.

WHY. Each row has its own little buttons sitting on top of it — the checkbox, the arrow, the +, the clock, the ⋮. A row only accepts a drop while the pointer is on the row; the moment it passes over one of those buttons, the row underneath stops accepting. When you grab low on the left and drag straight up, you travel up a whole column of checkboxes, so the row at the top never gets a chance to say yes. Dragging by the name works because the middle of the row is clear all the way up.

THE FIX. While a row is being dragged, those little buttons stop taking the pointer, so the path up is plain row the whole way. At rest nothing changes — the checkbox still ticks, the ⋮ still opens the menu, the name still renames.

I also checked the priority tree for the same bug. It does not have it: the tree accepts a drop differently. But the tree DID have one more dead spot — the little square marker beside each row — so that is fixed here too, and every column of a tree row now drags.

Proven both ways: the new gate fails 3 of 15 checks on the build you are running, and passes all 15 on the fix. The full suite is green too — 56 checks, 0 failures, including the 175-check regression run.
